title: Use singular aspects for item schemas and correctly pluralized aspects for collections

facts.note: Task text mentions artifact/schema naming or cardinality.

facts.note: Whether a schema is an item or a collection, and whether a plural is correct English, needs judgement or a dictionary-backed detector.

fires: An artifact's schema describes a single item and its aspect is (or would be) written in the plural.
An artifact's schema describes a collection and its aspect is singular or wrongly pluralized.
An existing artifact name is checked or touched and its aspect number does not match its schema cardinality.
A schema changes between item and collection without its aspect changing (schema-only cardinality change).
A collection aspect is formed from an irregular, uncountable or compound noun.
doesNotFire: Naming of things that are not artifacts with an aspect segment (e.g. prose headings, code variable names).
Edits that touch no artifact name and no schema item/collection shape.

given: An artifact name's aspect refers to a schema that is either a single item or a collection (e.g. in a plan, wagon, WMBT, acceptance, doc or the schema itself)
when: the planner writes, renames or checks that aspect, or the schema's item/collection shape changes
then: Use the singular aspect for an item schema and the plural aspect for a collection schema, following English pluralization rules.
prefer: Irregular: English irregular form (analysis->analyses, policy->policies, datum->data, index->indices, child->children).
Uncountable: explicit suffix (config vs config.collection; data.item vs data.items).
Compound: pluralize the primary noun (button-group->button-groups, session-state->session-states).
avoid: Plural aspect on an item schema, or singular aspect on a collection schema.
Naive 's' plurals of irregular nouns (analysiss, policys, childs).
An uncountable collection aspect without an explicit suffix (e.g. bare config or data for a collection); a bare item like config is fine.
Pluralizing a non-primary noun of a compound name.
why: Cardinality is read from the aspect's singular/plural form, so correct plurals keep the item-vs-collection signal reliable.
evidence: Every artifact aspect in scope is singular when its schema is a single item and plural when its schema is a collection.
Each plural aspect follows the applicable rule: regular +s, English irregular form, explicit suffix for uncountables, or pluralized primary noun for compounds.
verifier_detail: Pluralization categories (term 'pluralization' = how to form the plural aspect): regular: add 's' (fragment->fragments, color->colors); irregular: English irregular forms (analysis->analyses, policy->policies, datum->data, index->indices, child->children); uncountable: use explicit suffix (config vs config.collection; data.item vs data.items); compound: pluralize the primary noun (button-group->button-groups, session-state->session-states).

Detector compares the aspect's grammatical number with the schema shape (item vs collection), checking existing as well as new/renamed names and schema-only shape changes; flag irregular nouns pluralized with plain 's'. For uncountable nouns, a collection aspect MUST carry an explicit collection suffix (config.collection, data.items); flag any uncountable collection aspect without one, even if it is otherwise distinguishable from the item. Accepted patterns: bare item + suffixed collection (config / config.collection) or suffixed item + suffixed collection (data.item / data.items).
